ccflow-celery provides a public, domain-neutral Celery-backed evaluator for ccflow callable models. It owns Celery app configuration, task serialization, worker execution, task routing, result handling, and Celery-specific operational documentation. Shared graph semantics, checkpoint models, retry policy definitions, and ETL run metadata should live in ccflow or ccflow-etl when they apply beyond Celery.

Implemented: CeleryEvaluator, CeleryGraphEvaluator, Celery app configuration, task dispatch, task-side model/context reconstruction, and a Fibonacci example. Partial: serialization hardening, result backend strategy, task routing, cancellation, timeout propagation, and integration with generic ETL retry/checkpoint metadata. Missing: opt-in integration tests for worker execution, production-oriented deployment docs, and guidance for large results that should not be materialized through Celery result payloads.
Depends on ccflow and Celery. May consume generic ETL metadata from ccflow-etl if the contract remains scheduler-neutral. Must not depend on finance packages or application-specific packages.

Default tests should run without a live broker by using eager/in-memory Celery modes or mocks. Tests that require Redis, RabbitMQ, or a real worker should be opt-in and skipped by default. Note This library was generated using copier from the Base Python Project Template repository.
